message.content:
Logistic regression is a statistical method used for binary (two‑class) classification problems.  
It models the probability that a given input belongs to one of two classes using a logistic (sigmoid) function applied to a linear combination of the input features.

Mathematically, for an input vector \(x = (x_1,\dots,x_n)\) and parameters \(\beta = (\beta_0,\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)\),

\[
p(y=1 \mid x) = \frac{1}{1+\exp\!\bigl(-( \beta_0 + \beta_1x_1 + \dots + \beta_nx_n )\bigr)} .
\]

The coefficients \(\beta\) are estimated by maximizing the likelihood of the observed data (or equivalently minimizing the cross‑entropy loss). Once fitted, the model outputs a probability; a threshold (commonly 0.5) is then used to assign class labels. Logistic regression is widely used because it is simple, interpretable, and works well when the relationship between predictors and the log‑odds of the outcome is approximately linear.
